Blood on Their Hands: Murder, Corruption, and the Fall of the Murdaugh Dynasty.

By Mandy Matney and Carolyn Murnick. Read by Mandy Matney. Nov. 2023. 10.5hr. HarperAudio, DD, (9780063269248) . REVIEW. First published January 1, 2024 ( Booklist ).
True crime fans will no doubt be familiar with the saga of the Murdaugh family and their stranglehold on the rather convoluted justice system in their little corner of South Carolina’s low country. And most of those who have heard the Murdaugh story will also be familiar with author Mandy Matney, the small-town journalist who broke early parts of the story on the Murdaugh Murders Podcast. Her investigations led to the exposure of decades of crime and corruption by Alex Murdaugh and his cronies and ended with his conviction for the murder of his wife and youngest son. Matney is also taking aim at the “good ol’ boy” system that is alive and well not just in law enforcement/justice but in media coverage of the powerful. The book is a behind-the-scenes account of getting the story of a lifetime while also trying to build her own future. Matney, who frankly addressed listeners who had a problem with her vocal fry on each podcast episode, has come a long way since the early days of her recording from her kitchen table with her dog sitting close by. Matney’s story and voice are recommended for true crime and memoir listeners.
— Jennifer K

Throughout the myriad developments in the case, Matney has found the national press coverage to be “eye opening.” While she’s seen “a lot of really great journalism,” she acknowledges that she’s also been disappointed with reporters who “take the easiest, goriest, most salacious angle of the story and roll with it,” which is “the opposite of what I want to do.”
Cognizant of the swirling sea of media being produced about the family—books, documentaries and more—Matney and co-author Carolyn Murnick decided to frame their offering as her own “memoir based on four years of reporting,” a sort of story-behind-the-story that provides new material for even Matney’s most faithful podcast fans. It’s meant to be inspiring to other journalists, and, as Matney notes, “It’s the book that I would have wanted to have 10 years ago when I started my journalism career.”
